title: 1956 AHSME Problem 6
statement: In a group of cows and chickens, the number of legs was \(14\) more than twice the number of heads. The number of cows was:

solutions.text:
Counting two legs for every head accounts for both legs of each chicken and two of each cow’s four legs. Thus every cow contributes exactly two of the \(14\) extra legs. Hence the number of cows is \[ \frac{14}{2}=7. \]

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Twice the number of heads already accounts for two legs per animal
Each cow contributes two additional legs beyond that baseline
